title: Irenaeus of Lyons
lead: Irenaeus, who as a boy heard Polycarp at Smyrna, later led the church at Lyons in Gaul and wrote Against Heresies, while Eleutherius was bishop of Rome (3.3.3), one of the main early sources on Polycarp, on the New Testament writings and on the teachers the church rejected. Jerome calls him 'a presbyter under Pothinus the bishop who ruled the church of Lyons' and later his successor (Lives of Illustrious Men 35).

sections.b: In a letter to Florinus, Irenaeus recalled: 'I am able to describe the very place in which the blessed Polycarp sat as he discoursed', and how Polycarp spoke of 'his intercourse with John and with the others who had seen the Lord' (Eusebius, Church History 5.20.6, NPNF). In Against Heresies 3.3.4 he tells that Polycarp was appointed in Smyrna by apostles, visited Rome under Anicetus, and called Marcion 'the first-born of Satan'. The copyists' notes at the end of the Martyrdom of Polycarp say their text was copied 'from the papers of Irenaeus' (Martyrdom of Polycarp 22:2).
